notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Blue strips on both sides of the plate, and the front plate is noticeably short. The pair is unique.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Triangular white bollards with a black top, a red reflector on the front and a white one on the back.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Very common: a solid white edge line on each side with no centre line. Less usual in other Mediterranean lands.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Guardrails often come doubled and carry red front reflectors; Spain uses yellow ones.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Guardrails usually finish with the rail flattening, widening and bending away from the road.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Lots of round concrete poles, unusual for the Mediterranean; the commonest top is a concrete trident.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Wooden poles commonly wear a small white sticker.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Many double consonants, lots of i, accents ì é à, words mostly ending in vowels; street signs say "via".

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Direction signs are blue with white arrows and ALL CAPS text. Motorway signs are green with a white and green border.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: The backs of road signs are very often black or dark grey.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Kilometre markers are white squares: a Roman numeral on top (hundreds of metres) over an Arabic one (kilometres).

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Road numbers start with SS, SR or SP: state, regional or provincial road.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Chevrons are white arrows on black, as also in Spain, Greece and Albania.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Pedestrian sign shows five stripes and a plain figure with no belt. Street signs are white with a thin blue border.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Urban "passo carrabile" signs show a no-parking symbol, with the town name at the top.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Pastel stone houses with terracotta roofs and wooden shutters split in two that open sideways.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Mediterranean scenery: farmed rolling hills and forested mountain valleys.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: German-bilingual signs in a mostly German-speaking northern area.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: French on signs in a northwest alpine valley; street signs often pair "via" with "rue".

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Slovene bilingual signs appear near the eastern border with Slovenia.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Completely flat plain, often hazy from poor air quality; rice is grown in its western and central parts.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Olive groves, bright rock walls and red soil in the southeast heel; southeast Sicily looks similar.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Round cone-roofed stone houses called trulli are unique to one southeastern valley, around Alberobello.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Arid, hilly farmland with rocky mountains; cacti and, in the east, citrus groves; Etna looms over the east.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Grey rocks poking from the ground, especially in the northeast; Sicily is drier.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Many buildings use irregular unpainted brown-grey stone; northeast Spain has a similar look.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Large white-walled buildings with wooden details in the northern alps.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Solid wooden shutters with black metal hinges are typical of the northeast.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Dark volcanic rock, many cacti and yellow lichen on islands off Sicily's coast, such as the one southwest of it.
